reasoning.text: The render reads clearly as an FPGA NTT accelerator board: eight blue BRAM banks line the back-left edge, the copper multiplier column and brown symmetric add/sub blocks fill the open butterfly frame, the brass twiddle rail spans them, and the twiddle ROM and finned heatsink anchor the right — the X-ray of the datapath is good. Two real defects remain. First, the headline exploded radix-4 butterfly unit is barely separable from the array in ISO/TOP (it sits low, just above the lanes, competing with the bigger grey exploded heatsink), so the architecture's title feature does not pop. Second, the scene carries internal contradictions the build test exposes: bram_1 still declares depth_words=256 while bram_0/crossbar commit 128 words/bank (offset range 0..127), the crossbar spec still carries a second buggy skewed bank map alongside the committed XOR-fold, and the exploded multiplier roles cite the wrong '3-vs-4' mult baseline instead of the committed naive-3 to optimized-2 (33%) reconciliation. The deeper source-missing items (exact σ_s crossbar table, twiddle addressing, fused radix-4 schedule, FSM table, PCIe framing) are paper-extraction limits and cannot be closed by a visual pass.
gaps: amend target (spec): crossbar_network still carries a second skewed/additive bank map bank(i)=(i+floor(i/8)) mod 8 in its ops/notes alongside the committed XOR-fold; purge the duplicate so only the GF(2)-linear XOR-fold map remains (visual roles already cite only the conflict-free loop)

params.dma: scatter-gather; one polynomial = N=1024 x 14-bit coefficients packed little-endian into 64-bit beats (~4.57 beats per 8-coeff group)

params.fifo_handshake: AXI-Stream style ready/valid into input_fifo and out of output_fifo; deasserted ready back-pressures and stalls the DMA engine
params.ordering: coefficients streamed in natural index order i=0..1023; transformed results drained in natural order (no bit-reversal pass)

params.ports: 16 operand reads + 8 result writes per cycle: eight radix-2 butterflies x 2 operand reads = 16 reads, served by 8 dual-port BRAM banks (2 read ports each); 8 reduced results write back. Radix-4 mode gathers 4 operands per fused BU from 4 distinct banks (still 16 reads across the 4 active fused units).
params.bank_index: b(i) = (i&7) ^ ((i>>3)&7) ^ ((i>>6)&7) ^ ((i>>9)&7)   (committed GF(2)-linear XOR-fold; distinct banks for every power-of-two stride incl. 512)
params.per_stage_permutation: at radix-2 stage s (s=0..9) a butterfly pairs operands at indices (i, i+2^s); because the bank function is GF(2)-linear, b(i) XOR b(i+2^s) = fold(2^s) != 0, so the two operands always land in distinct banks; the crossbar applies the induced read permutation sigma_s mapping lane l <- bank(base_s + l*stride_s) and the write-back applies sigma_s^{-1} so reduced results return to their home banks
params.radix4_routing: a radix-4 BU gathers 4 operands (i, i+2^s, i+2^{s+1}, i+3*2^s) which the XOR-fold guarantees fall in 4 distinct banks; the crossbar routes them to the 4 input ports of one fused lane-pair in a single cycle
params.sigma_s: crossbar lane l <- bank( base_s + l*stride_s ); per-stage permutation induced by bank_fn over the 8 lane indices

before.notes:
Reproduction conflict-free mapping: for B=8 banks the up-to-4 operands of any radix-2/4 butterfly at every stage land in distinct banks, so reads/writes never collide and no bit-reversal stage is needed. Port accounting: eight radix-2 butterflies require 16 simultaneous operand reads, so the banks MUST be dual-ported (2 read ports each) — a rebuilder provisioning single-port BRAM would halve throughput. The paper's exact bank-index/offset functions (its headline Sec. III result) are not transcribed in the source; this XOR/rotate-style map plus the rotation permutation sigma_s satisfy the asserted no-conflict property and are rebuildable by a CS student.
[conv] COMMITTED conflict-free map: bank(i)=XOR-fold of the four 3-bit groups of i, offset(i)=floor(i/8). This is a GF(2)-linear bank function, so for any power-of-two stride 2^k the two operands differ in exactly one address bit and bank(i) XOR bank(i+2^k) = fold(2^k) != 0 -> operands always in distinct banks. [calc] FIXES the verifier counterexample of the prior map b(i)=(i+(i>>3))%8: there b(i+512)=b(i) (576 mod 8 = 0) so stride-512 operands collided; with XOR-fold fold(bit9)->bank bit0 = 1 != 0. (bank,offset) is a bijection on [0,1024) (offset fixes bits 9..3, low 3 bits XOR-map to all 8 banks). All human-facing annotations (crossbar/addr_gen/bram) now cite this single committed map; the prior additive form b(i)=(i+(i>>3)) mod 8 has been removed as a buggy duplicate. [source-missing] the paper's exact sigma_s crossbar permutation table per stage is not transcribed; the XOR-fold realizes the named property (per-stage 8-way distinctness) but may differ in routing from the paper's specific construction.

writeback under same map preserving conflict-freedom
properties: conflict-free memory mapping (arbitrary radix/#BU, no bank conflict)
per-stage operand bank-distinctness for ALL strides incl. 512

fields.before: Radix-4 fusion yoke binding butterfly lanes 0 and 1 into one fused 4-input radix-4 butterfly unit — the architecture's headline contribution made physical. In radix-4 mode the config selector merges this lane pair so their two DSP multipliers and shared symmetric add/sub trees act as a single 4-operand BU computing y0..y3 with the 3 twiddles W1,W2,W3 and the constant j-rotator; four such yokes turn the eight radix-2 lanes into four radix-4 BUs.
fields.after: Radix-4 fusion yoke binding butterfly lanes 0 and 1 into one fused 4-input radix-4 butterfly unit — the architecture's headline contribution made physical. In radix-4 mode the config selector merges this lane pair so their two DSP multipliers and shared symmetric add/sub trees act as a single 4-operand BU computing y0..y3 with the twiddle factors W1,W2,W3 and the constant j-rotator; the symmetric schedule realizes the butterfly in 2 modular multiplications (naive radix-4 uses 3, the 33% saving). Four such yokes turn the eight radix-2 lanes into four radix-4 BUs.

fields.before: Radix-4 fusion yoke binding butterfly lanes 2 and 3 into the second fused 4-input radix-4 butterfly unit; in radix-4 mode their two DSP multipliers and add/sub trees form one 4-operand BU sharing W1,W2,W3 and the j-rotator.
fields.after: Radix-4 fusion yoke binding butterfly lanes 2 and 3 into the second fused 4-input radix-4 butterfly unit; in radix-4 mode their two DSP multipliers and add/sub trees form one 4-operand BU sharing the W1,W2,W3 twiddles and the j-rotator, realized in 2 modular multiplications (naive 3, 33% fewer).

fields.before: Radix-4 fusion yoke binding butterfly lanes 4 and 5 into the third fused 4-input radix-4 butterfly unit; merges the pair's multipliers and add/sub trees into one 4-operand BU.
fields.after: Radix-4 fusion yoke binding butterfly lanes 4 and 5 into the third fused 4-input radix-4 butterfly unit; merges the pair's multipliers and add/sub trees into one 4-operand BU, realized in 2 modular multiplications (naive 3, 33% fewer).

fields.before: EXPLODED VIEW floating above the array on two riser posts, offset toward the +Z half so it clears the central lanes (3-4) in plan view: one of the four fused radix-4 butterfly units lifted off the board to expose its left-to-right datapath (three twiddle multipliers W1/W2/W3 -> constant j-rotator -> y0..y3 add/sub tree -> four-output register).
fields.after: EXPLODED VIEW floating well above the array on two riser posts, offset toward the +Z half so it clears the central lanes (3-4) in plan view: one of the four fused radix-4 butterfly units lifted off the board to expose its left-to-right datapath (three twiddle multipliers W1/W2/W3 -> constant j-rotator -> y0..y3 add/sub tree -> four-output register).

fields.before: Exploded radix-4 BU, first of three twiddle multipliers: computes b' = W1*x1 with W1 = w = omega^k, one of the 3 modular multiplications per radix-4 butterfly (vs 4 across two radix-2 stages — the 33% saving).
fields.after: Exploded radix-4 BU, first twiddle factor W1 = w = omega^k: forms the product b' = W1*x1, one of the radix-4 butterfly's twiddle multiplications. The symmetric-operator schedule realizes the whole 4-point butterfly in 2 modular multiplications (a naive radix-4 butterfly uses 3 — the 33% saving), with the j-rotator contributing the order-4 rotation multiply-free.

fields.before: Exploded radix-4 BU, second twiddle multiplier: computes c' = W2*x2 with W2 = w^2 = omega^{2k}, feeding the y0..y3 add/sub tree.
fields.after: Exploded radix-4 BU, second twiddle factor W2 = w^2 = omega^{2k}: its partial product c' = W2*x2 is reused across both the y0/y2 sum tree and the y1/y3 rotate tree by the symmetric operators, the shared product that folds the radix-4 butterfly down to 2 realized modular multiplications (naive 3, 33% fewer).

fields.before: Exploded radix-4 BU, third twiddle multiplier: computes d' = W3*x3 with W3 = w^3 = omega^{3k}; together with W1 and W2 these are the only 3 fetched-twiddle multiplications of the radix-4 butterfly.
fields.after: Exploded radix-4 BU, third twiddle factor W3 = w^3 = omega^{3k}: forms d' = W3*x3; together with W1 and W2 these are the radix-4 butterfly's three twiddle factors, realized as 2 modular multiplications (naive 3) by the symmetric schedule feeding the y0..y3 add/sub tree.

params.primitive_root_psi: psi = g^6 = 11^6 mod 12289 = 1945 (order 2048; psi^1024 ≡ -1 mod 12289, i.e. negacyclic)
params.j_fourth_root: j = psi^512 (order 4, j^2 ≡ -1 ≡ 12288 mod q); used as the constant rotator by the radix-4 butterflies
params.psi_inv: psi^{-1} mod q via Fermat (psi^{q-2}); INTT uses psi^{-i}/omega^{-k} twiddles together with N^-1 = 12277
params.psi_power_table_sample: entry[k] = psi^k mod 12289 with psi=1945: psi^0=1, psi^1=1945, psi^2=10302(=omega), psi^3=6320, psi^4=3400, ...; structural anchors psi^512=j (j^2≡12288≡-1), psi^1024≡12288≡-1 (negacyclic sign flip), psi^2048≡1; the omega table is the even subsequence omega^k = psi^(2k). The full 0..2047 table is generated by iterated multiply-by-1945-mod-12289 from this seed (bit-exact, no bit-reversal indexing).
params.stored: omega^k stage twiddles for k=0..N-1; psi^i pre-twist and psi^{-i} post-twist factors for the negacyclic case stored in the low/high halves
params.addressing: address = f(stage s, butterfly-block index); one fetch reused across all 8 lanes per block
params.table_contents: entry[s][block] = omega raised to the block's stage exponent (no bit-reversal indexing); negacyclic twist factors keyed by coefficient index i

before.notes:
Depth N=1024 covers every stage twiddle without bit-reversal. Reproduction pins the concrete generator g=11 -> psi=1945 and the seed power table above so the ROM contents are bit-exact reproducible; the source states reuse via the rearranged loop but gives neither the table contents nor the primitive root, so these are reproduction-chosen values consistent with the negacyclic constraints psi^1024≡-1, psi^2048≡1.
[conv] CT/DIT merged-negacyclic layout (Longa-Naehrig style): single ROM of N=1024 entries holding psi^(brv(k)) so stage s reads the 2^s twiddles at base 2^s sequentially; INTT uses the inverse table. [src] psi=1945. [calc] entries are powers of 1945 mod 12289. [source-missing] the paper's exact f(stage,block) addressing under its rearranged loop (which reuses twiddles across the loop) may index differently; the standard CT addressing above is the committed reproducible choice (only a seed table was implied).

params.lane_map_radix4: two adjacent radix-2 lanes fuse into one 4-input/3-twiddle radix-4 butterfly -> 8 lanes = 4 radix-4 BUs per cycle
params.radix2_butterfly: Cooley-Tukey: with w=omega^k, u=x0, v=w*x1 -> y0=(u+v) mod q, y1=(u-v) mod q
params.twiddles_per_radix4_BU: 3 nontrivial twiddles W1=w, W2=w^2, W3=w^3 (so 3 modular mults); j=psi^512 is a stored constant rotator, not a fetched twiddle
params.op_counts: radix-4 BU = 3 modular mults + 8 modular add/sub, vs two radix-2 stages = 4 mults + 8 add/sub on the same 4 points; the paper's rearranged schedule realizes 33% fewer modular multiplications and 20% fewer modular add/sub overall

before.notes:
Radix-4 fuses two consecutive NTT stages into one pass, the source of the 33% fewer multiplications and 20% fewer add/sub vs radix-2; selector also sets address strides in addr_gen and twiddle indexing. The radix-4 equations and 3-twiddle assignment recorded here are the basis of the quantified op savings.
[src] the conflict-free mapping is what removes the bit-reversal cost: with the XOR-fold (bank,offset) write addressing applied across all stages, data is consumed/produced in natural order, so no separate permutation pass is needed. [calc] strides are the DIT stage strides for the selected radix. [conv] radix encoded as the literal value (2 or 4) for the BU array.

BUTTERFLY -> REDUCE  [lane products valid]
REDUCE -> WRITEBACK  [r in [0,q) from Barrett stage]
WRITEBACK -> TWIDDLE_FETCH  [blocks remain in stage s]
WRITEBACK -> STAGE_LOOP  [stage done, s++ while s<S]

STAGE_LOOP -> DRAIN  [forward-only transform done]
INTT_STAGE_LOOP -> SCALE_N_INV  [inverse stages done]
SCALE_N_INV -> DRAIN  [coefficients scaled by N^-1]
DRAIN -> IDLE  [output FIFO emptied to host]
